chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan and Fadala from al-Ala' said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I shaved my head and sacrificed [the animal] while I was in the state of Tamattu', and I anointed my head with henna.' He said: 'Yes, provided you do not touch anything of perfume.' I said: 'And I wear the qamis [seamless garment] and cover my head [with the edge of the ihram]?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Before I perform Tawaf around the House?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.الْحِنَّاءِ: Henna, used here for anointing the head
key_terms.الْقَمِيصَ: A type of shirt or seamless garment
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٌ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, in a separate year

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible acts after shaving the head during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the transitional state of the Mu'tamir during the interval between Umrah and Hajj, specifically addressing the permissibility of resuming normal attire and grooming after the initial shaving. It highlights the scholarly distinction that while general perfume is prohibited, the application of henna is allowed, reflecting the practical ease granted to pilgrims in the sacred months. The ruling confirms that these acts of preparation can occur prior to the completion of the Tawaf al-Ifadah, emphasizing the sequential nature of Hajj rites.
